name: all_requirements
description: Returns a paginated slice of requirements across the corpus, optionally filtered by module. Designed for the dashboard's default Requirements tab view when no specific analytical question has been asked yet — just 'show me what's in the graph'. Returns module, id, heading, object_type, level, and verification status so the card component can render a full requirement summary without a second round-trip.
when_to_use: Fire this when the user wants to browse the corpus without a platform / standard / impact anchor. Natural phrasings: 'show me the requirements', 'list all requirements', 'what's in FCC', 'browse the corpus'. For platform-filtered views use platform_requirements. For module-level health use module_coverage.

parameters.name: module_name
parameters.description: Optional module filter. If provided, only requirements whose module property matches are returned. Pass null or omit to return across all modules. Expected values today: FCC, FMS, AUTO, GPS, INS (5 loaded modules, 284 total requirements).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of requirements to return. Keep small for snappy UI (default 50).

cypher:
MATCH (r:Requirement)
WHERE ($module_name IS NULL OR r.module = $module_name)
  AND (r.object_type IS NULL OR r.object_type = 'Requirement')
OPTIONAL MATCH (r)-[:VERIFIED_BY]->(t:TestProcedure)
WITH r, count(DISTINCT t) AS test_count
RETURN r.id                     AS requirement_id,
       r.module                 AS module,
       r.heading                AS heading,
       r.text                   AS text,
       r.object_type            AS object_type,
       r.level                  AS level,
       r.platform               AS platform,
       r.priority               AS priority,
       r.status                 AS status,
       r.safety_classification  AS dal,
       r.compliance_standard    AS standard,
       CASE WHEN test_count > 0 THEN 'COVERED' ELSE 'GAP' END AS verification_status
ORDER BY r.module, r.id
LIMIT toInteger(coalesce($limit, 50))
notes: This is the 'default feed' template — no analytical reasoning, just corpus browsing. The two-part WHERE handles the null-module-filter case without needing a separate untagged Cypher. The filter on object_type excludes Heading and Table rows that slipped in during parsing, so the card list stays clean. When platform_requirements returns empty (the graph lacks explicit Platform nodes or per-requirement ALLOCATED_TO edges), fall back to this template with a module filter.
